# MycoHalo

The goal of MycoHalo is to ...

## Installation

You can install the development version of MycoHalo like so:

 
```{r}
largest <- which.max(areas)

largest
```
 # Build clean plate mask
```{r}
plate_mask <- labels == largest

EBImage::display(plate_mask)


```
 
# label again
```{r}
labels <- EBImage::bwlabel(mask_clean)

max(labels)

```
# component size
```{r}
features <- EBImage::computeFeatures.shape(
  labels
)

head(
  sort(
    features[, "s.area"],
    decreasing = TRUE
  ),
  20
)
```
```{r}

mask_clean <- EBImage::opening(
  mask,
  EBImage::makeBrush(
    size = 7,
    shape = "disc"
  )
)

mask <- gray > 0.25

EBImage::display(mask)

```


```{r}

moments <- EBImage::computeFeatures.moment(labels)

moments

```

# colony segmentation may become easy using:

```{r}
plate <- detect_plate(plate)
plate

labels <- EBImage::bwlabel(mask)

max(labels)

features <- EBImage::computeFeatures.shape(labels)

features[, "s.area"]


```


## morphological operation

```{r}
mask_clean <- EBImage::opening(
  mask,
  EBImage::makeBrush(
    size = 15,
    shape = "disc"
  )
)

mask_clean <- EBImage::fillHull(
  mask_clean
)

EBImage::display(mask_clean)
```

## Example

This is a basic example which shows you how to solve a common problem:

```{r example}
library(MycoHalo)
labels <- EBImage::bwlabel(mask)

features <- EBImage::computeFeatures.shape(labels)

areas <- features[, "s.area"]

areas
```

What is special about using `README.Rmd` instead of just `README.md`? You can include R chunks like so:

```{r cars}
summary(cars)
```

You'll still need to render `README.Rmd` regularly, to keep `README.md` up-to-date. `devtools::build_readme()` is handy for this.

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo = FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

In that case, don't forget to commit and push the resulting figure files, so they display on GitHub and CRAN.
